svg.title: V-JEPA 2: feature prediction during pretraining, action-conditioned prediction after adaptation
svg.metadata: V-JEPA 2 paper · Sections 2–4: https://arxiv.org/html/2506.09985v1 | Pretraining · EMA and target branch: https://github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2/blob/main/app/vjepa/train.py | Action-conditioned training code: https://github.com/facebookresearch/vjepa2/blob/main/app/vjepa_droid/train.py

text.tspan: V-JEPA 2: feature prediction during pretraining, action-conditioned prediction after
Two branches meet in a feature-prediction loss.
V-JEPA 2 · action-free pretraining. A moving-average teacher supplies the target representation.

g.title: Two branches meet in a feature-prediction loss.
g.desc: V-JEPA 2 · action-free pretraining. A moving-average teacher supplies the target representation. The student encodes the visible context. A separate encoder sees the full video and follows the student by exponential moving average. Mask-location embeddings tell the predictor which missing regions to estimate from context features. The loss compares predicted and target representations. Gradients train the student and predictor; the target branch uses stop-gradient. Dashed connection: parameter update by EMA, not a video-feature connection. Pretraining is action-free. It predicts representations rather than reconstructing pixels.

text.tspan: Dashed connection: parameter update by EMA, not a video-feature connection. Pretraining is action-free. It predicts
Actions enter during a separate adaptation stage.
V-JEPA 2-AC · inference and planning after adaptation. Frozen image features feed an action-conditioned predictor.

g.title: Actions enter during a separate adaptation stage.
g.desc: V-JEPA 2-AC · inference and planning after adaptation. Frozen image features feed an action-conditioned predictor. Freeze the pretrained visual encoder. Encode the current context and the goal, while candidate actions and robot state supply control inputs. The adapted predictor rolls features forward. A distance to the encoded goal scores the hypothetical outcome. CEM refines action candidates inside model predictive control. Execute the first action, observe again, and repeat. The action-conditioned predictor is trained on robot trajectories with teacher-forced and two-step rollout L1 losses. The paper’s robot configuration uses 16×16×1408 encoder features and a 24-layer, 16-head, width-1024 predictor with 7D action/state inputs. It is not the action-free pretraining predictor.
